source: George, Walker & Monster (2019) Does strategic planning improve organizational performance? A meta-analysis (read via Wikipedia, Strategic planning)
finding: The meta-analysis behind this subfield is George, Walker and Monster 2019. Planning helps performance, most for effectiveness. The effect depends on formality (analysis), comprehensiveness (many options before choosing) and stakeholder management.
numbers: Almost 9,000 organizations (as reported on the page). No effect size on the page.
quote: many strategic options before selecting the course to follow
limits: Second-hand summary. The primary paper was not opened (Wiley returned 403).
agent_relevance: Names the moderator we can copy: comprehensiveness = many options before selection. Maps to S3 generate-then-select.

source: McKinsey Quarterly (2006) Improving Strategic Planning: A McKinsey Survey (read via Wikipedia)
finding: Many firms had a formal planning process but did not use it for their most important decisions.
numbers: No figure given on the page.
limits: Second-hand; the survey itself was not opened.
agent_relevance: A plan that is not used at the decision point is worth nothing: the scaffold must bind the final choice to the plan step.

source: Shea-Van Fossen, Rothstein & Korn (2006) Thirty-five years of strategic planning and firm performance research: a meta-analysis (AOM)
finding: Pooled planning-performance effect is positive but fragile to publication bias.
numbers: 39 studies, 74 effect sizes, 5,223 firms. Overall standardized mean difference 0.257 (p<.001). After trim-and-fill: 0.109 (CI -0.235 to 0.242), i.e. not distinguishable from zero.
limits: Conference paper. Abstract only was read.
agent_relevance: Planning benefit may be overstated; test planning steps by ablation, do not assume.

source: Boyd (1991) Strategic planning and financial performance: a meta-analytic review. J Management Studies 28(4)
finding: Older meta-analysis: modest planning-performance correlations; author argues they understate the truth because of measurement error.
numbers: 29 samples, 2,496 organizations, nine performance measures.
limits: Abstract only. Exact r values not read.
agent_relevance: Same shape as the LLM story: modest average gain, noisy measurement.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting (ACL 2023)
finding: Telling the model to plan first, then solve, beats zero-shot 'think step by step'. Longer planning instructions (PS+) help more. Planning mainly cuts missing-step errors.
numbers: Text-davinci-003, six math sets, zero-shot average accuracy: CoT 70.4, PS 72.9, PS+ 76.7 (Program-of-Thought 73.5). CSQA 65.2 -> 71.9; StrategyQA 63.8 -> 65.4.
limits: One old model. Gains are a few points; the StrategyQA gain is only 1.6.
agent_relevance: A plain plan step is a cheap, positive-but-small lever, like the human meta-analysis.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve: error profile
finding: A plan prompt targets only one error type; calculation errors need extra instruction and misunderstanding stays the biggest.
numbers: Zero-shot CoT with GPT-3, error analysis of 46 GSM8K failures: semantic misunderstanding 27%, missing step 12%, calculation 7%.
limits: Single model, small sample of 46.
agent_relevance: A plan fixes missing steps, not wrong problem understanding: restate the problem (S1) before planning.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Generating several candidate thoughts per step and selecting among them (comprehensiveness) beats a single chain. Breadth matters: width 5 beats width 1.
numbers: Game of 24, GPT-4: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC k=100 9.0%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%.
limits: Toy task with a checkable answer. Many more calls than one chain.
agent_relevance: Closest machine analogue of option generation before selection, with a measurable breadth dose-response.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: sampling-only baselines
finding: Much of the gain from options comes from sampling alone; search plus a value step adds the rest.
numbers: Game of 24: IO best of 100 = 33%, CoT best of 100 = 49%, IO + refine k=10 = 27%, ToT b=1 = 45%, ToT b=5 = 74%.
limits: Same task and model as above.
agent_relevance: Cheap many-sample options reach 49%; structured selection reaches 74%. Both parts matter.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: selection step
finding: ToT uses the same LM to propose and to score candidates; BFS keeps the best b=5 per step.
numbers: b=1 gives 45%, b=5 gives 74% on Game of 24.
limits: Model-scored selection is the weak link per our guardrails; the final answer is checked only by the game rule.
agent_relevance: Replace model scoring with code checks wherever a check exists.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: scaling inference compute with repeated sampling
finding: Coverage (any sample correct) rises log-linearly with number of samples across four orders of magnitude. Turning coverage into accuracy needs a verifier.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct: 15.9% with 1 sample, 56% with 250 samples; single-sample state of the art 43%.
limits: Large gain only where answers are automatically verifiable.
agent_relevance: Many options only pays if selection is sound, matching the human moderator split.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: selection limits
finding: Without automatic verifiers, majority voting and reward models plateau beyond several hundred samples.
numbers: Plateau beyond several hundred samples (abstract).
limits: Full per-task curves not extracted.
agent_relevance: Cap the option count; past a point extra options buy nothing without a checker.

source: Jiang et al. (2025 v5) Self-planning Code Generation with LLMs (ACM TOSEM)
finding: A planning phase then an implementation phase raises code pass rate. Giving a ground-truth plan raises it far more, so plan quality is the limit.
numbers: HumanEval Pass@1: self-planning 60.3 (+25.4% relative to direct, +11.9% over CoT); CoT 53.9; ground-truth plan 74.4 (+54.7%).
limits: Gain grows with model size; weak at small scale. A few code benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Plan helps; a better plan helps about twice as much. Invest in plan quality and checking.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) On the planning abilities of LLMs
finding: Autonomous plan generation by LLMs is poor; an LLM suggestion helps human planners a little.
numbers: Best LLM (GPT-4) about 12% executable plans; average about 3%. Human with LLM suggestion 18 of 22 (82%) vs 17 of 23 (74%) without.
limits: Human-assist difference not significant per the paper. 2023 models.
agent_relevance: LLM alone is a weak planner; check plan content in code.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023): human baseline
finding: Humans do the same Blocksworld tasks far better than 2023 LLMs.
numbers: Human valid plans 78% (39 of 50); optimal among valid 89.7% (35).
limits: Preliminary human baseline.
agent_relevance: Gives a human reference line for machine planning tests.

source: Valmeekam, Stechly & Kambhampati (2024) LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs? (o1 on PlanBench)
finding: o1 is a large jump on PlanBench but still far from saturating it.
numbers: No figures on the abstract page; abstract only.
limits: Abstract page only; numbers not read.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models narrow, but do not close, the planning gap.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) Position: LLMs can't plan, but can help planning in LLM-Modulo frameworks
finding: Generate-and-test: LLM proposes candidate plans, external verifiers critique, loop back.
numbers: With VAL verifier back-prompting, Blocks World reaches 82% within 15 rounds; Logistics 70%; obfuscated Mystery Blocks World about 10%.
limits: Position paper; numbers come from Valmeekam et al. 2023. Fails where the LLM cannot propose plausible candidates.
agent_relevance: Template for our schema: model fills the option slot, code verifies and selects (G2, G3).

source: Stechly, Valmeekam & Kambhampati (2025) Chain of Thoughtlessness? CoT in planning
finding: Planning-style prompts help only when very specific to the problem class; gains collapse as problems grow past the examples.
numbers: Blocksworld table-to-stack, GPT-4: zero-shot 3.83%, stacking-specific prompt 59.3%. Self-consistency lowered performance on these prompts.
limits: Simple domain, three models; authors read it as pattern matching.
agent_relevance: A generic make-a-plan prompt may not transfer; test per task family.

source: Stechly et al. (2025): prompt table
finding: General algorithm prompts were weaker than narrow ones.
numbers: Columns GPT-4-Turbo / Claude-3-Opus / GPT-4: zero-shot 19.1 / 9.96 / 3.83; zero-shot CoT 21 / 10.34 / 4.98; Universal Algorithm 37.1 / 37.1 / 51.3; Stacking prompt 40.6 / 24.5 / 59.3.
limits: One domain, three models.
agent_relevance: Keep plan templates specific to the task family.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) NATURAL PLAN, Google DeepMind
finding: Natural-language planning (trips, meetings, calendars) is hard and collapses with size. Self-correction and few-shot do not fix it reliably.
numbers: Trip Planning: GPT-4 31.1%, Gemini 1.5 Pro 34.8%, GPT-4o 3.7%, GPT-3.5 7.3%; all below 5% at 10 cities. Meeting: GPT-4 47.0%. Calendar: Gemini 1.5 Pro 48.9%. Gemini 1.5 Pro shots 1 to 800: 2.7% to 39.9%.
limits: Full-information setting; 2024 models.
agent_relevance: Difficulty rises sharply with number of constraints: split large plans into small checked pieces.

source: Xie et al. (2024) TravelPlanner
finding: Multi-constraint real-world planning is nearly unsolved by agents with ReAct, Reflexion or CoT.
numbers: Two-stage: GPT-4-Turbo with ReAct final pass rate 0.6%, others 0%. Sole-planning best final pass about 4.4% (table text scrambled). Gap between two modes up to over 30 points.
limits: Per-row attribution of the 4.4% figure is uncertain from the extracted table. 2024 models.
agent_relevance: Strategies that work on small tasks did not rescue complex planning; hard constraints need code checks.

source: Goh, Kos & Goel (2026) Knowledge Model Prompting Increases LLM Performance on Planning Tasks
finding: A structured task-method-knowledge scaffold lifts a reasoning model on symbolic planning.
numbers: PlanBench Blocksworld, o1: Random 31.5% -> 97.33%; Mystery 74.3% -> 83.3%.
limits: One benchmark, OpenAI models, preprint.
agent_relevance: Structured planning scaffolds can give very large gains on strong models.

source: Goh, Kos & Goel (2026): weaker model
finding: Scaffold benefit depends on the model: o1-mini regressed on Mystery.
numbers: o1-mini Mystery 19.1 -> 16.83; o1 Mystery 74.3 -> 83.3.
limits: Single paper.
agent_relevance: Test each scaffold on the target model before adopting it.

source: Backlund & Petersson (2025) Vending-Bench
finding: Long-running business simulation: some models earn money but variance is huge and runs derail; not caused by full context.
numbers: Five runs each. Mean net worth: Claude 3.5 Sonnet $2,217.93 (min $476), o3-mini $906.86, Human (5 hours) $844.05, Gemini 1.5 Pro $594.02, GPT-4o mini $582.33.
limits: Human baseline is one run. Small simulated business.
agent_relevance: Plans without recovery fail on long horizons: re-plan on a failure signal (G1).

source: OPPO AI Agent Team (2026) EcoGym
finding: Eleven LLMs on three business simulations; no model wins all; models are weak at either strategy or execution.
numbers: Operation DAU: Claude-Sonnet-4.5 1595.00 vs human experts 1,404. Vending net worth: Claude-Sonnet-4.5 1843.62 vs a Gemini-3 row near 11,272. Context k=32 to 1024: no consistent gain.
limits: Row-to-model mapping in the extracted table is partly scrambled; per-model values approximate.
agent_relevance: Strategy quality and execution quality are separate; more memory does not buy better strategy.

source: Wang & Zhang (2025) From Bits to Boardrooms: BusiAgent
finding: Role-based CEO/CTO/CFO agents claim to beat baselines in problem analysis and task assignment.
numbers: 100 experts, 941 ratings. Claimed +122% problem analysis, +284% task assignment, Welch p<0.05. BLEU 18.7 -> 23.4 in a translation-startup replay.
limits: Weak evidence: expert ratings of own system, synthetic simulation, BLEU as business outcome; uses many more tokens.
agent_relevance: Do not copy. Example of a strategic-planning role loop with unconvincing measurement.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking (Apple)
finding: On controllable planning puzzles, reasoning models collapse past a complexity threshold and cut effort near collapse; plain models win at low complexity.
numbers: Three regimes: low complexity plain models win; medium reasoning wins; high both reach zero.
limits: Abstract-level; later criticism about token limits not opened.
agent_relevance: Match planning effort to difficulty; supports doubt-on-signal (G1).

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Language Agent Tree Search (LATS)
finding: MCTS-style search over candidate actions with LM value and reflection, using environment feedback, improves agents.
numbers: HumanEval Pass@1 92.7% with GPT-4; WebShop +22.1 with GPT-3.5 (as stated in the text).
limits: Needs environment feedback; many calls.
agent_relevance: Options plus external feedback beats option generation alone (G2).
